translation_notes: notation change only: the 14 namespace_term accesses become prefixed names (OWL_NS.SymmetricProperty -> owl:SymmetricProperty, RDF.type -> rdf:type) and the `OWL_NS = Namespace(...)` line is absorbed by `@prefix owl: <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#> .`. Every prefixed name here occurs *outside* an island (inside a tuple and inside list literals), which the disambiguation rules handle without a single parenthesis change.

the rdflib import block is kept verbatim even though RDF/RDFS/Namespace become unused, so that the diff shows only the term notation. BNode/Literal/URIRef/Variable were already unused in the extracted region.

mechanical-draft bug fixed: the draft derived the prefix name from the Python variable (OWL_NS -> `owl-ns:`) and emitted `owl-ns:SymmetricProperty`. Per the language reference a prefix that is not a Python identifier is usable *inside islands only*, so `owl-ns:` outside a g{} would not have been recognised; the prefix is named `owl:` instead. The draft had also inserted the @prefix statements inside the parenthesised `from rdflib import (...)` list.

demo harness added identically to both representations: AllProperties is a generator yielding infixowl Property objects, which the driver cannot compare directly. The harness consumes it over a small OWL vocabulary that exercises both base-type branches and the prevProps de-duplication, prints the listing, and leaves the graph (mutated by Property.__init__, 8 -> 11 triples) at module level.

context shim: `Property` is defined elsewhere in the vendored infixowl module; it is imported from the installed rdflib's own rdflib.extras.infixowl, whose Property has the same constructor signature. Identical for both representations. Importing the vendored copy from the corpus checkout was rejected because that checkout would shadow the installed rdflib package.
